newsitem.title: USA: Consumer incomes, spending up in January.
newsitem.headline: Consumer incomes, spending up in January.

text.p: Consumers increased their spending briskly in January as personal incomes kept growing, the Commerce Department said on Monday, adding momentum to the economy's expansion as 1997 began.

Spending increased 0.7 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.3 trillion -- the strongest pickup in monthly spending since a 0.9 percent gain last October -- after a slim 0.2 percent December rise.
Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources rose 0.3 percent to $6.65 trillion following a 0.7 percent December increase.

The gains in both incomes and spending were slightly stronger than anticipated by Wall Street economists, who had forecast an increase of 0.1 percent in incomes and an increase of 0.6 percent in spending.
Despite the strong pace of January spending, savings held steady at 5.4 cents out of each dollar earned, the same as in December.

The department said that January incomes were boosted by cost-of-living adjustments in federal transfer payment programmes as well as by pay raises for federal civilian and military employees. Excluding special factors, personal incomes increased by less than 0.1 percent in January.

Gains in personal income, which includes wages and salaries as well as income from sources such as dividends, interest and businesses, are essential for funding consumer purchases, which fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.
The spending increases were widespread, reflecting earlier reports that showed relatively strong retail sales as well as a steadier pace of new-car sales.
Spending on durable goods, which includes cars, rose to an annual rate of $643.2 billion in January from $632.5 billion in December.
Spending on nondurables like food and gasoline climbed to an annual rate of $1.572 trillion from $1.567 trillion in December while spending for services rose to $3.08 trillion from $3.06 trillion.
Private-sector wages and salaries slipped to an annual rate of $3.098 trillion from $3.108 trillion in December.
Payrolls of manufacturing companies fell to a rate of $690.2 billion in January from $692.9 billion in December.
